title: Qwen3.5 9B uncensored arrives with DeepSeek-V4-Pro reasoning, refuses 3 of 100 prompts
summary: Qwen3.5 9B uncensored arrives with DeepSeek reasoning capabilities
detailed: The Qwen3.5 9B uncensored model was released on Hugging Face, utilizing DeepSeek-V4-Pro reasoning data and stripped of refusals using Heretic 2.0.0.dev0.
The model refuses only 3 out of 100 prompts, compared to 100 out of 100 for its starting version, and weighs 5.63 GB for the Q4_K_M GGUF format.
The underlying SFT training set by user Jackrong includes approximately 250,000 math and STEM examples generated by DeepSeek-V4-Pro, while user xtools-at applied the Heretic tool.
This matters because it provides developers with a lightweight, highly capable, and virtually unfiltered 9-billion-parameter model built on Alibaba's open architecture.
sentences: Qwen3.5 9B uncensored is a 9 billion parameter model that reasons like DeepSeek-V4-Pro and refuses almost nothing.
In the model card published on Hugging Face on October 30, 2026, it turns down 3 prompts out of 100, against 100 out of 100 for the version it started from.
The full repository name is DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B-UNCENSORED-heretic .

The model has been online for a week, and these past few hours it is bouncing around social media with promises bigger than the model card: a platform "in meltdown", zero loss of intelligence, and use on any computer.
Some of it holds up, some of it does not.
Four names are needed to get oriented.
Hugging Face is the site where developers, universities and companies publish AI models, a sort of GitHub for models.
Qwen3.5 is Alibaba's family of open models.
DeepSeek-V4-Pro is one of the models from DeepSeek (the Chinese lab known for releasing its weights; the launch of the V4 family is covered separately) and here it plays the teacher.
Heretic is the open source program that strips the refusals out of an already trained model, meaning the answers along the lines of "I can't help you with this request".
The full weights are on Hugging Face under the Apache 2.0 license, with no access request.
For the lightweight 5.63 GB Q4_K_M file there is mradermacher's GGUF repository, to load in llama.cpp or in the programs built on it.
No account is needed to download.
The first is Qwen3.5-9B, Alibaba's open model that everything starts from.
The second was built by the user Jackrong, who published DeepSeek-V4-Pro-Qwen3.5-9B on July 19, 2026.

Inside are about 250,000 examples of math and science (the acronym is STEM) generated by DeepSeek-V4-Pro in "Max Effect" mode, used for supervised training (SFT, meaning question and answer pairs) and then for a light reinforcement learning phase called GSPO.
The third link, from October 30: the user xtools-at ran that model through Heretic 2.0.0.dev0 (a development version) and uploaded the result.
That calls for two corrections to the viral posts.
The model is not a "hybrid" in the sense of two networks fused together, because DeepSeek-V4-Pro only lent the answers to imitate and its weights are not inside.
And the 250,000 samples do not cover programming.
The model card talks about math and STEM and states that no data was used for code.
The model refuses 3 prompts out of 100 by the measure the model card reports, while the version it started from refuses 100 out of 100.
That is the count Heretic computes by default, run by the author on prompts the model card does not list.
The result is nothing exceptional among the Qwen3.5 9B models put through Heretic.
Other variants already in circulation claim 2 out of 100 (against 86 for the original) or 6 out of 100 .
That the starting point shifts from 86 to 100 shows how much the numbers depend on the prompt set chosen.
Next to the refusals the model card shows the KL divergence, a number that measures how far the modified model's answers drift from the original's on harmless prompts.
For the original it is 0 by definition.
It measures how much the answers change, not how much the model can do.
That distinction matters in the next point.
The model card does not say so, and the numbers cannot say so.
Every benchmark reported is Jackrong's, run on the version with the refusals still active.
For the unfiltered version xtools-at published no capability evidence, only refusals and KL.
The starting model's data is interesting all the same.
On GSM8K (grade-school math problems) the model card reports 94.50%, averaged over four runs.
On MMLU-Pro, with 500 questions per subject drawn from math, physics and chemistry, the average is 90.53% against 89.60% for Qwen3.5-9B.
The clearest edge is restraint.
The model spends 2,858 reasoning tokens per question (the small chunks of text it produces while thinking) against 4,425 for the base Qwen, about a third fewer.
GSM8K and MMLU-Pro were measured with different engines, and the model card itself warns that the scores should not be compared with each other.
On code, which the posts take for granted, the model card records small, preliminary gains.
The idea of a 9B that beats everyone at programming finds no basis in the text.
On this point the posts are right.
In the mradermacher GGUF repository , which specializes in conversions, the Q4_K_M file (the format read by llama.cpp, quantized to 4 bits) weighs 5.63 GB.
It drops to 3.83 GB with Q2_K and climbs to 9.53 GB with Q8_0, while the uncompressed file reaches 17.92 GB.
The original BF16 weights sit in four files totaling about 18.9 GB.
The memory needed for the context has to be added to the file size, so on a computer with 8 GB you are working at the limit.
Real uptake, but not overwhelming.

The main repository counts 772 downloads over the last 30 days and more than 160 likes, while the conversions circulate far more, with 32,366 downloads for the i1 variant , 7,418 for the standard one and 1,703 for a third repository (Hugging Face API data as of November 7).
A fourth repository appeared today as well, in NVFP4, the 4-bit quantization designed for the newest Nvidia cards.
Anyone who wants to try a similar file locally will find the steps in the guide to installing uncensored models on Mac and Windows .
There is no trace of a Hugging Face outage tied to this model.

The repository has been public since October 30, is not gated behind an access request and has not been disabled; according to IncidentHub , the platform's last recorded incident dates to September 24, 2026.
The context, if anything, is a different one.

As we reconstructed in the piece on the ban on the first uncensored models , in October the platform removed a few individual repositories, a GLM-5.3 built for cyberattacks and an abliterated Kimi K2.7 Code.
This one, as of November 7, is still up.
Heretic 2.0 came out on November 1, 2026 and makes Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA), developed specifically for the program, its default method.
The project's README promises a technical preprint soon, so the inner workings are not yet fully documented.
What is new is covered in our piece on Heretic 2.0 and ARA .
The model card, for its part, lists the parameters used (intervention on layers 9 through 24 of the network) without explaining what they do.
The method retrains nothing, it edits the weights directly, as we explained in the guide on uncensored Qwen and Heretic .
